Lessons.Title: Arcs and Sectors
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Derive central-angle fraction formulas for arc lengths and sector areas using a known radius and degrees.
At central angle θ degrees, length L=(θ/360)2πr Use θ within [0,360]
Area A=(θ/360)πr² Use square units For positive minor θ, arc exceeds chord

Authentic task: Create an original segmented-circle diagram and justify fraction formulas; teacher reviews measurements. Teacher rubric (0–4): correct circle or radian model, valid assumptions, exact calculations/angle interpretation, and well-supported explanation. Diagrams and reasoning require teacher scoring.
Source: Illustrative Mathematics Geometry First Edition (2019–2021), Unit 7 Lesson 8, CC BY 4.0. Independently written examples; no copied art or restricted assessment.

KeyConcepts.Title: Sector area

KeyConcepts.Title: Arc vs chord
KeyConcepts.Definition: Straight chord 2r sin(θ/2) may differ from arc length
KeyConcepts.Rule: For positive minor θ, arc exceeds chord

Known central angle determines arc fraction θ/360 Solve fraction × circumference Ask one additional variable

Lessons.Title: Angles, Arcs, and Radii
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Use similarity of circles to show arc-length divided by radius depends only on central angle, anticipating radians.
For equal central angle, L/r is invariant across circles Both L and r scale equally
Central angle θ degrees yields L/r=πθ/180 Direct proportionality in θ Ratio is dimensionless and defines radians

Authentic task: Draw two similar circles and compare same-angle arcs with explicit proportional proof; teacher scores. Teacher rubric (0–4): correct circle or radian model, valid assumptions, exact calculations/angle interpretation, and well-supported explanation. Diagrams and reasoning require teacher scoring.
Source: Illustrative Mathematics Geometry First Edition (2019–2021), Unit 7 Lesson 10, CC BY 4.0. Independently written examples; no copied art or restricted assessment.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unitless quantity
KeyConcepts.Definition: Arc length and radius must have identical units to cancel
KeyConcepts.Rule: Ratio is dimensionless and defines radians
KeyConcepts.Example: Length 3 cm over radius 2 cm gives 1.5

Lessons.Title: A New Way to Measure Angles
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Define radian measure of a central angle as arc length divided by radius and derive 180°=π radians.
For arc length s and circle radius r>0, θ=s/r radians Length units must match
A full circumference has s=2πr so θ=2π Half revolution π 90°=π/2,45°=π/4

Authentic task: Measure an original circular arc and radius and explain quotient as invariant angle; teacher checks chart. Teacher rubric (0–4): correct circle or radian model, valid assumptions, exact calculations/angle interpretation, and well-supported explanation. Diagrams and reasoning require teacher scoring.
Source: Illustrative Mathematics Geometry First Edition (2019–2021), Unit 7 Lesson 11, CC BY 4.0. Independently written examples; no copied art or restricted assessment.

Lessons.Title: Radian Sense

Quarter turn π/2; half turn π; full turn 2π Check angle placement on diagram Use exact expressions before approximation

Lessons.Title: Using Radians
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Derive s=rθ and A=(1/2)r²θ for a circular sector whose central angle θ is in radians.
s=rθ with θ in radians and r>0 Based on definition θ=s/r
A=(1/2)r²θ for 0≤θ≤2π, measured in radians Use area fraction θ/(2π) Use θ/(2π) for sector fraction

Authentic task: Students derive sector formula from area fraction then construct three sectors; teacher reviews derivation.
